source.title: HomeAdam: Adam and AdamW Algorithms Sometimes Go Home to Obtain Better Provable Generalization
source.authors: Feihu Huang; Guan-Yi Zhang; Song-Can Chen

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices. Some equations and figure contents are flattened or not numerically recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizer variants on held-out task performance and gives stability-based generalization bounds, using different methods from the mapped empirical optimizer comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative test accuracy or perplexity comparisons in Figures 2–5, but the supplied text gives no plotted values. The cited prior results and theoretical comparisons to prior bounds are not rows. Hyperparameters in Appendix E are setup details, not results.
record.test_reason: The paper uses Adam's reported generalization disadvantage to motivate new optimizers and reports their performance against baselines. Its textual results do not establish standard Adam versus SGD held-out performance, or recovery from that disadvantage under the interventions V4 names. Comparisons of stability upper bounds do not establish an ordering of actual generalization errors.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. More precisely, they claim smaller stability-based generalization upper bounds for HomeAdam(W), faster convergence bounds than square-root-free Adam(W), and improved experimental held-out performance. Smaller upper bounds alone do not prove smaller actual generalization errors.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes square-root-free Adam(W) and HomeAdam(W), which switches between adaptive updates and momentum-based SGD based on a threshold; experiments compare these with standard optimizers. The theoretical claims use algorithmic stability.
record.method_sensitivity: The algorithm variant and use of weight decay change reported held-out performance. Experiments vary task and model across CIFAR-10/VGG16, Tiny-ImageNet/ResNet34, WikiText2/8-layer Transformer and WikiText-103/24-layer Transformer.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that square-root-free Adam(W) and HomeAdam(W) outperform the comparison optimizers across four tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed optimizer variants improve held-out performance under the paper's selected settings.

fits_no_version.finding: HomeAdam(W) has higher image-classification test accuracy and lower language-model test perplexity than square-root-free Adam(W).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intermittent SGDM updates improve held-out performance relative to the paper's square-root-free adaptive baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: HomeAdamW has better held-out performance than HomeAdam on the reported tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoupled weight decay improves HomeAdam under the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper derives stability-based generalization upper bounds for its optimizer variants under stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HomeAdam(W) admits an O(1/N) expected generalization-gap upper bound under the theorem's assumptions and learning-rate conditions.

record.problems: Experimental comparisons are reported qualitatively in the supplied text, with results presented in figures whose numeric values are unavailable. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates for these comparisons. Its generalization theorems are stability bounds under stated smoothness, Lipschitz and variance assumptions, not direct measurements of training-to-test error gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No other separately recoverable result rows. Numerical values in Figures 2–5 cannot be read from the supplied text; the four aggregate comparison rows preserve the textual result statements.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Recoverable standard Adam-versus-SGD comparisons under limited tuning; broader tuning; standard AdamW or Adam-to-SGD recovery; and Adam's possible word-level language-model advantage. Appendix E lists selected settings but gives no tuning protocol.
Batch-size interventions under matched epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions. Different fixed dropout rates in different language models do not test dropout's effect.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps. Algorithmic stability bounds do not measure this relationship.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative performance directions are supported by Sections 6.1–6.2. The corrected states concern whether the rows establish a claim version, not whether those reported improvements occurred. Figures 2–5 lack recoverable values in the supplied text, and that omission is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
The comparisons do not report broad hyperparameter tuning, optimizer switching, or a word-level language-model result.
Large-batch effects and adaptations to epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties tracking the gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
